rival.why_confusable: Both locate nearby places from a city and a preference list.
rejected: Do not treat the repeated preference sentence as a second difference.

same_request.note: A request for a library does not make the store description true. A request that only says somewhere nearby can be read as either.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

cases.case_reason: A general unit conversion can be read as covering a currency conversion, so a cue would repeat the polynomial failure: both descriptions can be true of one currency request, and the contrast would read as an exclusion the sources do not state.

tools.no_cue_reason: Converts a value from one unit to another. Currency is a unit of value, so naming the currency tool as a rival would claim an exclusion the unit description does not state.
Converts a value from one currency to another. The other description already says it converts a unit. No cue is written.

cases.case_reason: Both tools predict from independent variables. One applies linear regression. The other applies Random Forest Regression.

tools.cue: Unlike random_forest_regression, which applies Random Forest Regression, this applies linear regression.

rival.axis: whether the prediction uses linear regression or Random Forest Regression
rival.why_confusable: Both make a prediction from the same kind of independent and dependent variables.
rival.why_this_rival: Only one other tool, and the action is a regression prediction.
rejected: The tree count belongs to Random Forest Regression. It is not a claim that linear regression lacks a forecast period.

same_request.note: A request that only says to predict from the variables can be read as either method. Linear regression is not Random Forest Regression.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

tools.cue: Unlike linear_regression, which applies linear regression, this applies Random Forest Regression.

rival.axis: whether the prediction uses Random Forest Regression or linear regression
rival.why_confusable: Both make a prediction from the same kind of independent and dependent variables.
rejected: Do not treat one regression method as a subclass the other description already covers.

same_request.note: The cue uses the source's own name for the forest method. A request that names one method makes only that description true.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

cases.case_reason: Both tools calculate interest from a principal, a rate, and a time. One is compound interest. The other is simple interest.

tools.cue: Unlike financial_simple_interest, which calculates simple interest, this calculates compound interest.

rival.axis: whether the interest is compound or simple
rival.why_confusable: Both calculate interest from an initial amount, an annual rate, and a time in years.
rival.why_this_rival: Only one other tool, and the function descriptions name the two interest types.
rejected: The compounding frequency n is an argument of compound interest, not a contrast that simple interest lacks a rate.

same_request.note: A request that only says interest can be read as either type. Compound and simple are alternate types, not a class and a subclass. The cue names the type.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

tools.cue: Unlike financial_compound_interest, which calculates compound interest, this calculates simple interest.

rival.axis: whether the interest is simple or compound
rival.why_confusable: Both calculate interest from an initial amount, an annual rate, and a time in years.
rival.why_this_rival: Only one other tool. The function description is the selection text.
rejected: The simple-interest time sentence says compounded. That conflicts with this function description and is not used as the axis.

same_request.note: The cue follows the function description, which says simple interest. It does not repeat the conflicting time sentence and does not say either tool rejects a principal.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

cases.case_reason: Both tools look up one religion. One returns core beliefs and practices. The other returns origin and founder.

tools.cue: Unlike religion_get_origin, which retrieves the origin and founder, this retrieves the core beliefs and practices.

rival.axis: whether the religion fact is the core beliefs and practices or the origin and founder
rival.why_confusable: Both retrieve a fact about a specified religion. A request that only names the religion can be read as either.
rejected: Do not drop practices or founder. Each description states both halves of its fact.

same_request.note: Beliefs and origin can both be true of a request that only names the religion. The cue keeps practices with beliefs and founder with origin, which is what the sources say.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.

tools.cue: Unlike religion_get_core_beliefs, which retrieves the core beliefs and practices, this retrieves the origin and founder.

rival.axis: whether the religion fact is the origin and founder or the core beliefs and practices
rival.why_confusable: Both retrieve a fact about a specified religion.
rejected: The parameter name religion is shared, so it is not the axis.

same_request.note: A request for the founder does not make the beliefs description true. The cue still separates the two facts when the request only names the religion.

propositions.note: Target fact cited by the cue.
Rival fact cited by the cue, from that tool's original description.
